html:
The Portuguese Inquisition was a church court set up in 1536 at the request of King John III to hunt heresy, above all among the New Christians, Jews forced to convert in 1497. It lasted until 1821.

Many Jews had fled to Portugal after the expulsion from Spain in 1492, only to be forcibly baptised. The Inquisition watched them for secret Jewish practice, seized property, and burned the condemned in public ceremonies called autos-da-fé. It also ran an inquisition in Goa in India.

Many New Christian merchant families fled to Amsterdam, Hamburg and the Americas, taking their trade networks with them. The Inquisition also censored books. The Marquis of Pombal ended the legal difference between Old and New Christians in 1773. Compare the Spanish Inquisition.
